title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Orienteering Control. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Orienteering Control
options.lineage: Swiss OL map: purple controls on a paper Landeskarte, description sheet, needle punch
options.thesis: Piles are controls. You are the triangle. Walk the course.
options.viewport: Phone PWA, GPS-centered paper course: you as start triangle, live piles as numbered purple circles, gone piles as afterimage ghosts, control-description strip at the bottom, one orange shutter to post.
options.risk: If the map tiles look like Google, it dies. The paper course is the product.

raised.raise: Gone piles stay as afterimage ghosts on the course, not a separate history page.
Every nearby pile is already present as a faint control; the closest one is struck. States snap, they do not tween.
Category is a letter-mark on the control, not a chip bar.
Markers jump in whole zoom steps; no blurry teardrop pins.
One safety-orange shutter posts. One live readout: metres or hours left.

options.label: Gratis Cardboard
options.lineage: Handwritten zu-verschenken signs taped to the pile
options.thesis: The listing is the sign people already tape to the stuff.
options.viewport: GPS map under torn cardboard tags: each pile is a marker-written card you can read at a glance; camera is another blank card.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on: the object itself as UI.

options.label: Zip-Tie Stockroom
options.lineage: Industrial streetwear grammar: quoted caps, zip-ties, hazard stripe
options.thesis: The street as a labeled stockroom. Live piles keep the orange zip-tie on.
options.viewport: Full-bleed map, piles as crate labels in straight quotes, 45° stripe under the selected pile, orange tie = still there.
options.case: Holds identification (everyone knows bulky-waste tape). Loses clarity: geography is weaker than a control course.
options.risk: Fashion costume if the quotes and stripes outrun the map.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The map as a scrolling transcript of piles.
options.case: Loses both: Swiss sidewalks do not identify with a machine room; a transcript hides geography.
options.risk: Hacker-movie UI on a street tool.

options.label: Cathode Gauze
options.lineage: Nixie / cathode numeral stack behind bronze mesh
options.thesis: Every pile present as a ghost; one struck glowing.
options.case: Loses both: no street identification; no map.
options.kept: All options present; snap, no tween.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.lineage: Letters as weather that carve landscape
options.case: Loses both: unreadable as a find-the-pile tool.
options.risk: Art piece, not an operate surface.

options.label: Emigre Bitmap
options.viewport: Poster-scale pixel labels on a map.
options.case: Loses both: design-nerd identification; specimen layout fights GPS.

options.label: Hardware Bench
options.lineage: Creator-hardware desk: bone keycaps, one orange key, knurled knob
options.thesis: The PWA as an instrument with one commit key.
options.case: Loses both: desk instrument, not sidewalk.
options.kept: One orange shutter. One live value.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean map app with teardrop pins, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: GPS map, blue loc dot, floating post button, pin sheet.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Apple/Google Maps with extra pins — the thing you said would feel wrong.
